title: PPO in practice: a diagonal Gaussian and the clips around it
brief: Score a continuous action with a diagonal Gaussian, keep a running mean and variance, and assemble one PPO step with advantage normalization, a clipped value loss, and a vectorized rollout.
hints: The log-probability of a diagonal Gaussian includes -0.5 * log(2π) on every action dimension. A ratio of two log-probabilities hides a constant that both of them drop.
Divide the variance by the count, not the count minus one. Chan's merge is mean_a + (mean_b - mean_a) * count_b / total, and the same weights on the summed squared deviations.
Normalize advantages by their own population standard deviation. Dividing by the standard deviation of the returns shrinks the policy step.
The value loss is the mean of the larger of the two squared errors. The clipped value is the old value plus the move, limited to ±clip_eps.
